behavioral_notes.observation: Tour completion is persisted as a per-user consumed-state, NOT a tour-level flag. consume(tourName) is an @api.model RPC that, only for internal users (env.user._is_internal()), links the calling user into user_consumed_ids (Many2many to res.users) via Command.link with sudo(). get_current_tour() then searches for tours where custom=False AND user_consumed_ids NOT IN the current user, gated on user.tour_enabled and _is_internal(), and returns the FIRST pending tour's JSON (sequence-ordered). This drives the automatic onboarding chain: each finished tour is recorded against the user and the next un-consumed tour is served. This consumed-membership semantics is invisible from field metadata alone.

tour_enabled is a stored computed Boolean (label 'Onboarding') depending on create_date. _compute_tour_enabled defaults it TRUE only when the user _is_admin() AND there are zero installed demo modules (search_count on ir.module.module demo=True) AND not modules.module.current_test — so onboarding tours auto-run for a fresh admin on a non-demo, non-test DB and are suppressed otherwise. switch_tour_enabled(val) is an @api.model RPC that flips the flag with sudo() and returns it; the JS debug 'onboardingItem' menu calls it to toggle tours and reloads the page.

ir.http.session_info() is overridden to push two keys into the bootstrap session payload: tour_enabled (the user flag) and current_tour (= get_current_tour(), the next pending onboarding tour JSON). The browser therefore learns at page-load which tour to auto-start without an extra RPC. Tours register TWO ways: (a) declaratively in the JS registry category 'web_tour.tours' (the normal path used by tests and product onboarding), and (b) as data rows in web_tour.tour/.step (custom/DB tours), exportable to a .js file via export_js_file() which serialises steps to a registry.category('web_tour.tours').add(...) attachment. _get_tour_json()/get_steps_json() camelCase server fields (tooltip_position -> tooltipPosition) into the JS step schema.

behavioral_notes.element: FRONTEND (static/src/js) — tour_service + dual macro engine (STRONGLY EMPHASIZED)
behavioral_notes.observation: The BULK of web_tour is OWL/JS, not Python: ~16 JS files / 5 XML templates across four asset bundles (web_tour.common/interactive/automatic/recorder). The core is the 'tour_service' (services registry), which exposes odoo.startTour and persists run-state in localStorage via tour_state.js (current_tour, index, config) so a tour SURVIVES page reloads/redirects. It validates each step against a StepSchema (trigger/run/content/timeout/tooltipPosition) and a TourSchema, then lazily loadBundle()s one of two engines by mode: (1) INTERACTIVE (manual) — TourInteractive drives a TourPointer OWL overlay that points at the live DOM trigger, attaches real DOM consume-event listeners (click/input/keydown/pointerdown/pointerup/drop, with autocomplete/dropdown/drag-and-drop special cases), and a MacroMutationObserver re-resolves triggers on every DOM mutation, even stepping backward() if an anchor disappears; on completion it fires a rainbow_man effect and RPCs consume() to chain the next tour; (2) AUTOMATIC (auto) — TourAutomatic compiles steps into a @web/core/macro Macro and uses hoot-dom (setupEventActions/queryFirst) to synthesise events headlessly with per-step timeouts/undeterminism checks — this is the HEADLESS TOUR RUNNER that integration tests (HttpCase.start_tour) execute. A run-command mini-language (e.g. 'click', 'fill(text)', 'edit', 'drag_and_drop(sel)', chained with &&) is parsed in getSubActions into low-level actions. A TourRecorder OWL overlay records user interactions into replayable steps. OWL components: OnboardingItem, TourPointer, TourRecorder; registry adds: fields:tour_start_widget, services:tour_service, views:tour_list; patch: TourHelpers.prototype. None of this is reverse-engineerable from Python/ORM metadata (gap #3).

classification.rationale: web_tour is cross-cutting firm IT infrastructure with no business object of its own — its only models (web_tour.tour/.step) describe the UI-guidance tooling itself, not any customer/product/order. It is a Porter support activity / Stabell & Fjeldstad 'support' value model: it creates no value in any single value chain, shop, or network; it is the user-adoption + test-automation framework layered on web (auto_install=true, category Hidden, depends only web) that EVERY app reuses. Its substance is the FRONTEND (~16 JS files, the tour_service plus the dual interactive/automatic macro engines, TourPointer and TourRecorder), with a thin Python tail (~396 LOC, 2 real models). APQC 8.0 'Manage Information Technology' fits on two counts: (a) user-adoption / application onboarding tooling = deploy/operate IT solutions and support users, and (b) the headless tour runner is test automation = develop and test software / manage IT quality — both squarely 8.x application-delivery. 13.0 'Develop and Manage Business Capabilities' was considered (tours teach users how to operate business capabilities) but rejected: 13.0 is governance/portfolio/knowledge-management of capabilities, whereas web_tour is a concrete running IT runtime (onboarding overlay + test engine) — its work is application delivery and quality, i.e. IT execution, which is 8.0, not capability governance.
